title: Resistance and the RL time
hook: Change resistance and predict RL time constant.
misconception: RL time constant doubles when resistance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply τ = L/R to compare RL time constant when resistance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal series RL circuit with fixed inductance, τ = L/R. When resistance doubles, RL time constant becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model τ = L/R; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal series RL circuit with fixed inductance, with a nonzero initial result. If resistance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on RL time constant?
recall.why: Apply τ = L/R under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
